title: Is there an aperiodic polyomino?
credit: Open problem as posed in A. Winslow, 'Some open problems in polyomino tilings' (DLT 2018); long-standing folklore (Golomb)
premise_risks: 'Polyomino' may be required to be simply connected in some sources; the Claim allows holes, which only makes the existence claim easier, so the vetter may prefer the simply connected version
existence proofs would likely be computer-assisted substitution arguments, heavy but finite in Lean
related to existing board items on hat/spectre tilings (M056, M057, N-117) but about a different tile class
plain: A polyomino is a shape made of unit squares glued edge to edge with no holes. In 2023 a single tile was found that tiles the plane only non-periodically, but it is built from kites, not squares. Is there a polyomino that tiles the plane (rotations and reflections allowed) but has no tiling that a translation maps onto itself?
math: A polyomino is a finite $P\subset\mathbb Z^2$ such that the union of the closed unit squares $c+[0,1]^2$, $c\in P$, is a closed topological disk. A tiling by $P$ is a set $\mathcal T$ of tiles $g(P)$, with $g(x)=Ax+b$, $A\in D_4\subset GL_2(\mathbb Z)$ and $b\in\mathbb Z^2$, that partition $\mathbb Z^2$. $P$ is aperiodic if some tiling exists but no tiling satisfies $\mathcal T+v=\mathcal T$ for any $v\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}$. Problem: does an aperiodic polyomino exist? Board Claim: yes. A proof that every polyomino that tiles also has a periodic tiling settles the problem negatively. (Variant: allow holes, i.e. require only that $P$ is edge-connected.)
review_note: Known: Translations only: a polyomino tiles iff it tiles isohedrally/periodically (Wijshoff-van Leeuwen 1984; Beauquier-Nivat 1991). k-anisohedral polyominoes known for k<=6 (Winslow survey, Open Problem 6 asks for k>=7). Aperiodic sets of 3 polyominoes (with isometries) known; aperiodic sets of 2 polyominoes unknown (Winslow, Open Problem 8); translational aperiodic sets of 7 polyominoes (Yang-Zhang arXiv:2412.17382). Undecidability for sets of 5 polyominoes (Ollinger 2009). Non-polyomino aperiodic monotiles: hat and spectre (Smith-Myers-Kaplan-Goodman-Strauss 2023/24, Combinatorial Theory). Survey: A. Winslow, 'Some open problems in polyomino tilings', DLT 2018.
